- **User's concern:** Autopay customers don't tip, and his technicians rely on tip income.
- **Analysis performed:** Claude reviewed 4,450 Jobber payment records since June 1; found autopay has 0.1% tipping rate (1 tip / $10 across 1,523 payments) vs hand-billed at 5.5% ($2,017 across 2,379 payments).
- **Financial impact quantified:** ~$7,300/year in lost tips from card/ACH payments alone; cash-tip data unavailable and likely higher.
- **Data segmentation:** Of 456 hand-billed clients, 70 (15.4%) have tipped at least once ($6,630/mo MRR), 386 (84.6%) never tipped ($52,297/mo MRR).
- **Campaign strategy proposed:** Suppress autopay conversion to only the 386 non-tippers; leave 70 tippers on invoices. Keeps 100% of tip income while converting 89% of hand-billed dollars.
- **Caveats noted:** 3.3-month analysis window may misclassify yearly tippers; recommends 12-month lookback before send to reduce false negatives.
- **Longer-term fix identified:** Build in-app "tip your tech" link in job-complete messages (Jobber/Roy build, not campaign) to enable tipping for autopay customers and address the structural gap.
